name: ahard_02_canonical_json
prompt:
from typing import Optional


def canonical_json(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """ Parse a document in a subset of JSON and return it in canonical form, or
    None if the document is invalid.
    The document is exactly one value, optionally surrounded by whitespace.
    Values: objects {"key": value, ...}, arrays [value, ...], strings, integers,
    true, false and null. Whitespace (space, tab, newline, carriage return) may
    appear before and after any value, comma, colon or bracket.
    - Strings are enclosed in double quotes. A raw newline inside a string is
      invalid. The only escapes are \\" \\\\ \\/ \\n and \\t; any other escape
      (\\u included) is invalid.
    - Integers: an optional '-', then one or more ASCII digits with no leading
      zero unless the digits are exactly "0" ("-0" is valid, "01" is not).
      Fractions and exponents are invalid.
    - Object keys are strings. Two keys that are equal after decoding escapes
      make the document invalid. Trailing commas are invalid.
    - Anything after the value other than whitespace is invalid; so is an empty
      or all-whitespace document.
    Canonical form: no whitespace at all; integers in plain decimal ("-0" becomes
    "0"); object members sorted by decoded key, in ascending character-code
    order; strings re-encoded with exactly these escapes: '"' as \\", '\\' as
    \\\\, newline as \\n and tab as \\t ('/' is written plainly).
    >>> canonical_json(' { "b" : [1, -0, "x\\/y"], "a": {} } ')
    '{"a":{},"b":[1,0,"x/y"]}'
    >>> canonical_json('[1, 2,]') is None
    True
    """
tests:
def check(candidate):
    assert candidate('{"b": [1, 2], "a": true}') == '{"a":true,"b":[1,2]}'
    assert candidate(' { "z" : { "y": null, "x": [ ] } , "a" : -0 } ') == '{"a":0,"z":{"x":[],"y":null}}'
    assert candidate('"tab\\there \\/ \\"q\\" \\\\"') == '"tab\\there / \\"q\\" \\\\"'
    assert candidate('[\n\t-12,\r\n"\\n", false\n]') == '[-12,"\\n",false]'
    assert candidate('42') == '42'
    assert candidate('{}') == '{}'
    assert candidate('') == None
    assert candidate('[1, 2,]') == None
    assert candidate('{"a": 1, "a": 2}') == None
    assert candidate('{"a" 1}') == None
    assert candidate('{1: 2}') == None
    assert candidate('[01]') == None
    assert candidate('[1.5]') == None
    assert candidate('"\\u0041"') == None
    assert candidate('[true] x') == None

def test_check():
    check(canonical_json)
